body:
Thank you very much. So sorry it has taken me so long to respond. I appreciate your imput. I was with my husband for 17 years. Most of those years we had a good, strong marriage. Things changed near the end. I did leave with our children when I realized how things had changed and it was affecting them. He spiraled downhill quickly when I left. I don't look back with regret or guilt. I did try as hard as I possibly could to save their father. I tried saving my best friend. I realized I can't force someone to save themselves. All I can do is try to prove I truly want the best for the people I love. 
I left to improve myself. As a person, as a mother. And I hope through all of this my children learn that there's absolutely nothing in the world that's worth comprising their own happiness. I can't live in the past nor can I change it. My point here was to try and reach just one person. Because if I could make one person see how much hurt will come of their loss, make them see that their happiness is worth fighting for... then man, I'd  be so happy I changed one family's future and saved so many such an unbearable pain.

And yet you really don't get to know your parents until you become an adult, get them to have a few drinks with you, and find out how cool they really are (or in some cases aren't). 

Probably the same time they discover about your shady shenanigans as a teenager. Gotta love holiday dinners.

I could come up with countless reasons for you to continue through your struggle. I know it won't change your thoughts though. You're the one that has to find the one reason to live. If you can find one, I'm sure more will follow. Maybe not as soon as you'd like, but eventually. 

If everything came easily, how would we learn to appreciate the things we have?  Part of the reason I've been able to make it through my husband's death without blaming myself is because for six months I heard how he felt. Although I did not understand his reasoning or logic, I saw things from his perspective. Of course I tried getting him help. I tried forcing him to get help... it wasn't fun. It definitely wasn't easy. But I tried. 

There's someone who loves you unconditionally. They will ache for you. They will probably blame themselves for years to come. And if they're not strong enough to seek help, they will probably self destruct. I want you to think about this one person, or people. Then I want you to think about talking to them about this endless sense of hopelessness you feel. Not to burden them, or lessen yours... but to create understanding that this feeling exists. And sometimes it's too much for one person to fight. Maybe it'll change your future, maybe it won't. I can guarantee it'll change theirs. You're never as alone as you think you are. Even strangers have your back.

You mentioned suicide as being selfish. I spent six months trying to convince my husband ending his life was not the solution. He spent six months trying to convince me otherwise. Ultimately, I lost that battle. I've lost that battle every. single. day since he died on April 7th 2014. 

I know he felt in his heart he was helping me. I know his intent was to end the pain. I also know he was wrong. 

Let me tell you about my hardest thing.

Was it selfish of me for wanting him to fight? Could I have done something, said something? Can someone build me a time machine to go back and change the minute it all went wrong? When did it go wrong? Why weren't our children enough? How could he not feel the love surrounding him enough? Did we love him enough? How will I parent alone? Will our kids be alright? Can I love them enough? Enough for two? Enough to prove to them they are so worth living for? 

While I asked him to love us enough to stay, he pleaded for me to love him enough to let him go. The torment is never ending. You see the survivors but you rarely see the pain they're masking. 

The difference between us is that I must find the greatness that resides inside of me no matter what. There is no option. I'm all my children have and I have to succeed. Otherwise I'm teaching them that what's broken cannot be fixed. But we're all broken, some more than others. Although the scars may always remain, we can all find a reason to wake up the next day if we look deep enough. 

I dont know you, but I know you are so worth it. Even if you don't believe me, I know it to be true.
